name: Use the High performance power plan
description: Activates the built-in High performance plan (created from the Windows template if hidden).
mechanism: Calls PowerSetActiveScheme with 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c. The plan keeps the minimum processor state at 100% on AC and disables several idle power-saving features.
benefit: Faster clock ramp-up and fewer latency spikes from deep idle states; most noticeable on older CPUs or OEM-modified Balanced plans.
drawback: Higher idle power, heat and fan noise. On modern CPUs Balanced often reaches the same peak clocks. Some Modern Standby laptops do not allow this plan.
recommendedFor: Desktops, and laptops while plugged in.
evidence: Built-in Windows power plan; behaviour documented in Windows power policy documentation.

name: Use the Ultimate Performance power plan (desktops)
description: Adds and activates the hidden Ultimate Performance plan.
mechanism: Duplicates the Ultimate Performance template (e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61) with powercfg and activates it. It removes most micro power-management latency.
benefit: Lowest possible power-management latency for workloads with frequent idle/busy transitions.
drawback: Noticeably higher idle power and heat; gaming gains over High performance are usually within noise. The created plan is deleted again on rollback.
evidence: Microsoft introduced the plan for workstations (Windows 10 1803). Benchmark before/after to confirm any benefit.

name: Disable USB selective suspend (plugged in)
description: Stops Windows from suspending idle USB devices while on AC power.
mechanism: Sets the active plan's 'USB settings › USB selective suspend setting' (2a737441-…/48e6b7a6-…) to 0 (Disabled) for AC. Battery behaviour is unchanged.
benefit: Prevents wake-up delays or dropouts of USB mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers after idle periods.
drawback: Slightly higher idle power when plugged in.
recommendedFor: PCs with USB input or audio devices that disconnect or lag after being idle.
evidence: Documented power setting (powercfg /q). Applies to the currently active plan only.

name: PCI Express Link State Power Management: Off (plugged in)
description: Keeps PCIe links (GPU, NVMe, network) out of low-power states on AC power.
mechanism: Sets the active plan's 'PCI Express › Link State Power Management' (501a4d13-…/ee12f906-…) to 0 (Off) for AC.
benefit: Avoids link wake-up latency; can fix micro-stutter with some NVMe drives and Wi-Fi adapters.
drawback: Higher idle power when plugged in. Battery behaviour is unchanged.
recommendedFor: High-end desktops and plugged-in gaming laptops.
evidence: Documented power setting. Firmware may override ASPM regardless of this value.
